mechanics.name: Corrective Action
mechanics.currentEffect: Start with 1/2/3 Tokens, up to 5. Completing a Great Skill Check grants 1 Token. While cooperating with another Survivor on an action that causes Skill Checks, a Token is spent when they fail a Skill Check to turn it into a Good Skill Check; their Aura is revealed to you for 6 seconds.
activation: Great Skill Checks grant a Token.
Cooperate with another Survivor on an action that causes Skill Checks when they fail.
Ends/deactivates when: Tokens are spent when converting a failed teammate Skill Check.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.3.0): Changed starting Tokens to 1/2/3 and maximum Tokens to 5.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Your tokens can convert a teammate's failed cooperative Skill Check into a Good one and reveal their Aura.
mechanics.tokenOrStackBehavior: Starts with 1/2/3 Tokens; gain 1 on Great Skill Check; maximum 5; spend 1 to convert a teammate's failed cooperative check.
specialInteractions: Applies to another Survivor performing a Skill Check during a cooperative action with you.

editorial.summary: Bank Tokens from Great Skill Checks and automatically convert a cooperating teammate’s failed Skill Check into a Good one.
useCases: Protect cooperative generators from a teammate miss.
Support newer players during heals or repairs without interrupting the action.
Replenish Tokens through your own Great Skill Checks.
counters: It only helps teammates performing a cooperative action with you.
Experienced teammates may rarely fail a Skill Check.
Tokens are wasted if the team mostly works separately.
pros: Starts with Tokens and can replenish them.
A prevented generator miss can save a large chunk of progress.
Passive once the co-op action is underway.
cons: Value depends on someone else making a mistake.
analysis: Corrective Action is one of those perks whose value depends more on the lobby than on the Killer. In a team with inconsistent Skill Checks, one prevented failure can save a meaningful amount of generator or healing progress.
The perk starts with Tokens and earns more from the user’s Great Skill Checks, so a mechanically strong player can effectively insure a weaker teammate during cooperative actions.
In experienced groups the trigger becomes rare, and the perk cannot create extra progress when nobody makes mistakes. That makes its ceiling practical rather than competitive.
It belongs above true gimmicks because the prevention is automatic and can save real time, but its value shrinks as the team improves.
editorial.verdict: Excellent insurance for co-op Skill Check mistakes, increasingly unnecessary as teammates become consistent. A useful teaching/support perk rather than a meta engine.
